robot.name: 1X EVE
robot.status_notes: Official 1X product page historically said EVE is available now and directs to contact sales. Multiple directories report EVE was deployed in customer facilities globally since 2022 and remains commercially active/industrial. No named customer evidence or current availability confirmation was found in the reviewed sources.

height.notes: Official 1X page lists 6 foot 2 inches (about 188 cm). Directories list 183 cm, 186 cm, and 188 cm; the official value is used here.

weight.notes: Official 1X page lists 192 pounds (about 87.1 kg). Directories list 83 kg and 86 kg; the official value is used here.

runtime.notes: Official 1X page says up to 6 hours on a 1-hour charge. IEEE ROBOTS guide lists 4 hours of operation and directories list 4-6 hours.

battery.notes: Battery capacity from IEEE ROBOTS guide. Official 1X page did not list battery capacity.

walking_speed.notes: Wheeled top speed, not walking. 9 mph converts to about 4.02 m/s; directories list 4 m/s (14.4 km/h).

degrees_of_freedom.notes: IEEE guide breakdown: neck 1 DoF; arm 7 DoF x 2; leg 6 DoF x 1; hand 1 DoF x 2; wheels 1 DoF x 2.

hands.description: Simple grippers, 1 DoF per hand, with 7 DoF per arm for manipulation.

items: High-resolution HDR cameras with panoramic views
Two front cameras and one rear camera

compute.description: Intel i7 for real-time control and Nvidia Xavier for AI inference (per IEEE ROBOTS guide).

availability.notes: Official 1X page says EVE is available now and provides a sales email. No public price or retail path was found; directories state no public pricing and current availability requires confirmation.

manipulation_dexterity.summary: Official 1X videos are titled for real-world manipulation and logistics, and Inverse reports a multi-robot demo of tidying an office, picking up a hoodie, and delivering drinks. EVE has 25 total DoF with 7 DoF per arm and 1 DoF grippers. No success rates or task durations are available.
caveats: No transcript for official manipulation/logistics videos; only titles were available.
Inverse reports the demo robots were not completely autonomous.

autonomy_task_execution.summary: 1X says EVE operates autonomously by default and can call in remote operators for shared autonomy. Inverse reports the 2024 multi-robot demo had someone behind the scenes telling robots when to switch tasks.
caveats: Company claim; no intervention logs or independent audit.
Shared autonomy means teleoperation can be involved; not clear how much was autonomous.

mobility_whole_body_control.summary: EVE uses a wheeled self-balancing base with multi-terrain wheels and a 4 m/s top speed, and can navigate corners and elevators. IEEE guide notes it can go down stairs but not up.
caveats: Wheeled platform; no independent mobility tests.
Stair-down claim from directory, not official video.

perception_scene_understanding.summary: Official page claims EVE can open doors, see people or objects from a distance, and navigate unstructured space. IEEE guide details HDR cameras (two front, one rear) and compute.
caveats: No independent perception benchmark.

human_interaction.summary: Inverse reports a voice-controlled natural language interface demo with multiple robots understanding office tidying commands; official page says EVE understands natural language.
caveats: The demo was not completely autonomous; someone switched tasks.
No conversational reliability metrics.

endurance_reliability.summary: Official 1X page lists 6-hour run time on 1-hour charge; IEEE guide lists 4 hours and 1.05 kWh battery; directories list 4-6 hours. No reliability or failure data found.
caveats: Runtime conflicting: 4h vs 6h.
No field reliability data.

human_environment_fit.summary: EVE is 188 cm and 87 kg with soft, organically-inspired mechanics and 1X claims it is safe for trained teams. It is a large wheeled robot and cannot go up stairs according to IEEE guide.
caveats: No safety certification evidence; warranty void up stairs.

deployment_commercial_proof.summary: Directories report EVE deployed in customer facilities globally since 2022, in guarding/monitoring and factories, but no named customer or metrics were found; official page says available now.
caveats: Unverified unnamed deployments.
Current availability unclear as 1X focuses on NEO.

accessibility_value.summary: No public price or retail path; 1X page provides contact sales email. Directories state no public pricing and confirmation required.
caveats: Contact sales only; no price, lease, or waitlist.
Not available to consumers.

evidence_items.title: EVE directory spec summary

evidence_items.verification_notes: Company claim; charge time not independently tested.

evidence_items.supporting_excerpt: Degrees of Freedom (DoF)25 (Neck: 1 DoF; Arm: 7 DoF x 2; Leg: 6 DoF x 1; Hand: 1 DoF x 2; Wheels 1 DoF x 2)

evidence_items.source_location: ROBOTS guide compute field; power field

evidence_items.title: IEEE guide stair capability caveat

evidence_items.source_location: ROBOTS guide Did you know? quote

evidence_items.title: RoboHuman global deployment claim

evidence_items.title: RoboLogAI contact sales status
evidence_items.claim: RoboLogAI tracks EVE as commercial/deployment with contact sales and lists logistics, security, healthcare, retail, teleoperation, and embodied AI training as use cases.
evidence_items.supporting_excerpt: EVE is a wheeled humanoid robot from 1X Technologies, tracked for logistics, security, healthcare support, retail service, teleoperation, and embodied AI training.

evidence_items.title: Inverse report on EVE multi-robot voice-command demo
evidence_items.claim: 1X revealed an Eve robot crew tidying an office with voice commands, chaining tasks like cleaning a coffee spill, picking up a hoodie, and delivering drinks; 1X said not completely autonomous.
evidence_items.notes: Media report of company demo; not a direct timestamped video review.
evidence_items.arena_relevance: Shows demonstrated multi-step household-ish manipulation and voice interaction, with human in loop caveat.
evidence_items.supporting_excerpt: 1X revealed the latest update to its Eve robot showing a small crew understanding a request to tidy up an office, linking together tasks like cleaning up a coffee spill, picking up a hoodie off the floor, and delivering drinks.
evidence_items.verification_notes: Inverse reports demo; says someone behind scenes tells robots when to switch tasks.

evidence_items.title: Missing disclosures
evidence_items.claim: No public price, named customer deployments, independent autonomy verification, success rates, intervention logs, safety certification, or current availability confirmation were found for EVE.
evidence_items.arena_relevance: Judges should reduce confidence on autonomy, deployment, and value.
evidence_items.supporting_excerpt: Gaps identified across all reviewed primary and secondary sources.
evidence_items.verification_notes: Absence of disclosure, not evidence of inability.

researcher_notes.short_verdict_for_arena: EVE is a wheeled humanoid with official specs and some commercial deployment signals, but evidence is mostly directory-level and no named customer or independent testing is public. Its shared-autonomy design and older platform status limit high-confidence capability scores.
strongest_positive_evidence: Official 1X page says EVE available now and can operate up to 6 hours on 1-hour charge.
Multiple directories report commercial deployments since 2022 in factories and guarding/monitoring roles.
Inverse reports a multi-robot voice-command demo of tidying an office with tasks like picking up a hoodie and delivering drinks.
weakest_or_missing_evidence: No named customer or deployment metrics.
No public price; contact sales only.
No independent autonomy verification; 1X says not completely autonomous in reported demo.
Official manipulation/logistics videos lack transcripts in this source set.
conflicting_claims: Height: 188 cm official vs 183/186 cm directories.
Weight: 87 kg official vs 83 kg directories.
Release year: 2020 IEEE guide vs 2018 ui44.
do_not_overclaim: Do not credit NEO or NEO Beta/Gamma capabilities to EVE.
Do not treat unnamed deployments as named commercial proof.
Do not describe EVE as fully autonomous based on the 1X page alone.
Do not state current availability without confirmation from 1X.

arena_prompt_summary.one_paragraph_summary: 1X EVE is a wheeled humanoid from 1X Technologies (Norway/US) with a self-balancing wheeled base, 188 cm, 87 kg, 15 kg payload, 4 m/s top speed, and 6-hour official runtime. It is designed for security, logistics, and embodied AI data collection, with 25 DoF, 1-DoF grippers, HDR cameras, and shared autonomy. The strongest evidence is an Inverse-reported 2024 multi-robot voice-command office-tidying demo and directory claims of unnamed customer deployments since 2022; the weakest areas are no named customer metrics, no price, conflicting specs, and no independent autonomy verification. EVE is older than 1X's NEO and current availability is unclear.
strongest_evidence: Official 1X page says EVE available now and 6-hour runtime with contact sales.
Inverse reports multi-robot voice-command demo of office tidying.
Directory reports deployment since 2022 in guarding/monitoring and factories.
weakest_evidence: No direct video transcript or independent verification.
